scope: session-bound — 2 documented cleanup BG side-effect incidents observed by parent agent during 2026-05-02 ~ 2026-05-03 cycle window
completeness_caveat: audit covers ONLY the 2 incidents the parent agent visually retained; older sessions and unobserved BG terminations are NOT included (raw#10 honest)

incidents.name: paradigm_d_mini_run_script_unlink
incidents.trigger_instruction: kill mini-run watchdog if step < 100, else preserve
cleanup_action_taken: SIGTERM to mini-run watchdog (clean — expected per branch)
cascading_failure_chain: training loop SIGTERM-trapped → entered post-loop teardown
post-loop teardown imports/refs back to /tmp/p9_paradigm_d_distill.py module
module file already unlinked → import/save calls silently failed
no error surfaced to cleanup BG (post-loop in disowned subprocess)
incidents.root_cause: ambiguous cleanup instruction — 'kill watchdog' vs 'delete script' vs 'full sweep' were not distinguished; cleanup BG defaulted to broader sweep (file unlink + SIGTERM) on the assumption that 'mini-run' implied disposable
incidents.secondary_cause: training script lived in /tmp (mutable, world-writable); no protection against unlink mid-run
incidents.observability_gap: cleanup BG did not verify pre-state (it never read step counter from trajectory.json before deciding); parent gave threshold (step < 100) but BG could not access it without separate channel

incidents.name: sentinel_50k_pid_gone_misinterpreted_as_completion
incidents.trigger_instruction: audit BG PID 1726340 status; report completed/running/failed

actual_state_at_trigger.log_tail_evidence: CUDA out of memory ... allocation failed

cleanup_action_taken: reported to parent: 'PID 1726340 NOT_FOUND, naturally completed'
cascading_failure_chain: parent did not investigate log → did not detect OOM
parent scheduled downstream consumer of expected-completed checkpoint
downstream consumer failed to find checkpoint → reported as 'savepoint missing'
wasted ~10 min of parent reasoning on misdiagnosis
lost_artifacts: no artifacts lost (run never produced any) — but parent state model was corrupted
preserved_artifacts: OOM stderr log (was on disk but not consulted)
incidents.root_cause: process death is not equal to process success — cleanup BG used a 1-bit signal (PID present / absent) where a 3-bit signal is required (running / clean-exit / crashed)
incidents.secondary_cause: no exit-code capture (background launch did not redirect $? or use trap); no log-tail check before declaring completion
incidents.observability_gap: absent verdict.json or PASS marker, the only available signals were exit code and log content — neither were checked

common_failure_modes.name: ambiguous_cleanup_verb
common_failure_modes.description: instructions like 'cleanup', 'kill', 'sweep', 'reset' do not distinguish: (a) signal the process, (b) delete the artifacts, (c) delete the source script, (d) delete the work dir, (e) all of the above

common_failure_modes.name: process_state_under_observation
common_failure_modes.description: PID-gone interpreted as success without inspecting exit code, log tail, or expected output artifacts

common_failure_modes.name: shared_mutable_resource
common_failure_modes.description: training script in /tmp (or any non-RO path) can be unlinked while mid-run; long-running scripts depend on their own file existing for re-import / lazy load

common_failure_modes.name: no_post_cleanup_audit_report
common_failure_modes.description: cleanup BG does not enumerate (a) what was killed, (b) what was preserved, (c) what was lost; parent infers state from absence of complaint

implementation_status: DESIGN_ONLY — no code or hook changes in this cycle
